[NADP.4.2.2] **Sync vs async work.** The cb runs on
the pump's stack per IARC.1.10 (no internal threads);
it must not block. It must not assert either: every call on the engine that
fired it returns `DS_ERR_STATE` ([RARC.13.16], [NCBK.1.2]). So the response fact
is asserted once that call has returned ([NCBK.6.4]). Two patterns:

- **Sync — fast services.** The adapter performs
  the work inline (a quick HA state-machine call,
  for instance), keeps the result, and returns DS_OK.
  Once the pump has returned, it asserts the response
  fact via `ds_engine_assert`.
- **Async — slow / latency-unbounded services.**
  The adapter queues the work onto its own runtime
  (asyncio task, thread pool, message broker
  publish) and returns DS_OK without asserting. The
  response arrives later when the queued work
  completes; the adapter's runtime then asserts the
  response fact from whichever thread the integrator
  pumps the engine on. A service declaring `no response`
  asserts nothing on success.
